analysis.evidence: Abram is the subject. The following verbs וַיָּבֹא וַיֵּשֶׁב describe his arrival and settlement at the oaks of Mamre, supporting the reading “moved his tent.”
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, agreeing with אַבְרָם.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֶּאֱהַל אַבְרָם, אַבְרָם names the subject who pitched his tent. The following verbs carry the same subject forward as Abram settles by the oaks of Mamre and builds an altar there.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: וַיָּבֹא וַיֵּשֶׁב recounts two successive actions. Abram arrived and then settled by the oaks of Mamre at Hebron.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ marks the Qal wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular. Abram is the subject.

analysis.evidence: וַיָּבֹא וַיֵּשֶׁב recounts Abram’s arrival and settlement. The phrase בְּאֵלֹנֵי מַמְרֵא identifies where he settled, at the oaks of Mamre.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Abram as its subject.
analysis.sense: to take up residence in a place

analysis.evidence: וַיֵּשֶׁב בְּאֵלֹנֵי מַמְרֵא locates Abram’s dwelling at the terebinths of Mamre. The following phrase אֲשֶׁר בְּחֶבְרוֹן places that landmark in Hebron.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ means “at.” The noun אֵלֹנֵי is masculine plural construct, with מַמְרֵא completing the phrase “the terebinths of Mamre.”
analysis.sense: A great tree or terebinth serving as a landmark.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause describing אֵלֹנֵי מַמְרֵא, the oaks of Mamre. בְּחֶבְרוֹן supplies the predicate, yielding “which are in Hebron.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew relative particle, uninflected and without prefix or suffix.
Hebrew adverb of place with no prefix or suffix.
